summary: The proposal is architecturally sound and most references check out correctly, but three MAJ defects require inline fixes before merge: (1) §3.1 uses a non-existent helper name 'scp_has_nonempty_string' instead of the actual 'scp_r_002_has_nonempty_string'; (2) §3.1's regex 'https://[^\s]+' is HTTPS-only while the parenthetical prose, §3.4, and §6 all intend HTTP+HTTPS ('https?://'), and the §10 HTTP question is consequently misclassified as [deferrable] when it changes match scope; (3) the §3.4 deny-rule comment falsely claims warn-baseline emission is handled by the warn rules below, when those rules only fire for suppressed findings — raw unwaived findings at warn-baseline require a distinct workflow mechanism. All three are inline-fixable without scope change.

findings.description: §3.1 match conditions reference the helper name 'scp_has_nonempty_string(e, "reason")' at lines 52 and 57. No such predicate exists in any policy file. The actual predicate defined in policies/SCP-R-002.rego (line 196) is 'scp_r_002_has_nonempty_string'. §3.4 (line 99), §5 (line 191), and §10 (line 329) all use the correct name. A Phase-2 implementer reading §3.1 as the canonical specification would reference a non-existent helper, producing a compile-time error (SCP-E002 fail-closed). This defect is in the normative spec text, not just the sketch.
findings.recommendation: Inline fix: replace both occurrences of 'scp_has_nonempty_string' in §3.1 (lines 52 and 57) with 'scp_r_002_has_nonempty_string'. The parenthetical at line 52 becomes: '(`scp_r_002_has_nonempty_string(e, "reason") == true`)'. The §3.1 coexistence note at line 57 becomes: 'SCP-R-004 does NOT fire (its second match condition `scp_r_002_has_nonempty_string(e, "reason")` is false)'.

findings.description: §3.1 line 53 states the URL pattern as 'https://[^\s]+' — this is an HTTPS-only pattern (no optional 's?'). The parenthetical on the same line says '(HTTP-or-HTTPS scheme, followed by at least one non-whitespace character)', which directly contradicts the regex shown. §3.4 (line 92) and §6.3 (line 251) both use 'https?://[^\s]+' (HTTP+HTTPS). Because the rule fires when NO URL is found, the difference matters: an HTTP-only URL 'http://internal-wiki.corp/dec-001' would pass under the §3.4/§6 regex but FAIL under §3.1's regex — different match scope. Additionally, §10 line 331 classifies the HTTP question as '[deferrable]' with the resolution 'accept both at v1.1.0'. Per RULE-TEMPLATE.md lines 155-158, '[deferrable]' is reserved for questions whose answer does not change match scope. The HTTP/HTTPS boundary changes which waiver entries fire the rule, so the question must be '[BLOCKING]'. The §10 resolution text already gives the correct answer ('accept both') — only the classification bracket is wrong.
findings.recommendation: Inline fix (two edits): (1) In §3.1 line 53, change the regex in the prose from 'https://[^\s]+' to 'https?://[^\s]+' so it matches both HTTP and HTTPS — consistent with §3.4 and the parenthetical; (2) In §10 line 331, change '[deferrable]' to '[BLOCKING]' on the HTTP question. The pre-resolved answer ('accept both at v1.1.0 — the regex `https?://` covers both') is already present and correct; only the classification bracket needs updating. No scope change: the resolution is already in the proposal.

findings.description: The §3.4 comment on the deny rule (lines 113-115) states: 'at warn baseline the workflow's annotation pipeline emits the warn variant via the warn rule below'. This is incorrect. The two warn rules that follow (lines 127-140) only fire when a finding is SUPPRESSED — either by an active waiver (first warn rule) or by rule-config disable (second warn rule). They do NOT fire on raw unwaived findings. At warn-baseline, the raw unwaived findings land in the deny set. To surface them as '::warning::' annotations, the workflow must either (a) add SCP-R-004 to a warn-class set so deny output is treated as warn-class, or (b) introduce a third warn rule that fires on raw findings not suppressed by waiver or rule-config. Neither mechanism is present in the sketch, yet the comment tells the Phase-2 implementer that the existing warn rules handle it — they do not. The 'Warn-baseline workflow integration' paragraph at lines 147-148 correctly identifies that the workflow needs changes, but is in tension with the inline comment that says the warn rules 'below' handle it.
findings.recommendation: Inline fix: replace the misleading comment on lines 113-115. Option A (preferred, consistent with existing SCP-R-001/002/003 pattern): change the comment to 'at warn baseline the WORKFLOW treats SCP-R-004 deny output as ::warning:: annotations rather than ::error:: — the deny rule fires on raw unwaived findings; the workflow step "Emit per-rule warning annotations" adds SCP-R-004 to the warn-class set (Phase-2 deliverable per the note below).' Option B: add a third warn rule that fires on raw unwaived non-disabled findings and emit it as the warn-baseline record — but this diverges from the SCP-R-001/002/003 pattern and requires corresponding workflow changes. Option A requires no code change to the sketch, only a comment fix, and aligns with the 'Warn-baseline workflow integration' paragraph that already correctly describes the mechanism.

findings.description: §3.3 annotation message format at line 68 specifies: 'SCP-R-004 waiver entry N (rule_id=<rid>, finding_id=<fid>): reason field must contain a decision-artifact URL ... Found reason text: "<truncated-reason>"'. The §3.4 raw_findings construction (lines 102-111) uses only 'sprintf("waiver entry %d reason field must contain a decision-artifact URL...", [index])' — it captures neither (a) the waiver entry's own rule_id/finding_id fields, nor (b) the truncated reason text. A Phase-2 implementer reading §3.3 as the annotation contract and §3.4 as the starting sketch will need to add two separate fields to the sprintf call that are not shown in the sketch. While a sketch is illustrative, this specific gap is in the section (§3.3) that defines the durable annotation contract adopters parse downstream.
findings.recommendation: Inline fix: update the §3.4 sprintf to include the rule_id/finding_id fields and the truncated-reason, OR add an explicit note in §3.4 that the sketch's message format is simplified and the Phase-2 implementation must match the §3.3 contract verbatim. Suggested note: '(Note: Phase-2 implementation must enrich this sprintf to match §3.3 annotation contract: include entry rule_id/finding_id via object.get(entry, "rule_id", "") + object.get(entry, "finding_id", ""), and truncate reason to 80 chars with trailing "…" per §3.3.)'.

findings.description: §3.1 lists 'The array is non-empty' as a separate explicit match condition (second bullet, line 49). The implementation guard 'scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload' does NOT enforce this — as verified in policies/SCP-R-002.rego lines 191-194, scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload returns true for BOTH non-empty arrays (count > 0) AND empty arrays (count == 0). The effective non-empty enforcement in §3.4 comes from the 'some index, entry in input' iteration idiom (no bindings for an empty array means no findings). A Phase-2 implementer who adds additional guards based on §3.1's specification ('use scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload to gate the non-empty check') would get wrong behavior — the predicate is intentionally true for empty arrays to allow SCP-R-002's per-entry checks to run. The non-empty condition in §3.1 is correct as behavior, but incorrectly attributed to the guard.
findings.recommendation: Inline fix: revise §3.1's second bullet from 'The array is non-empty' to 'The array is non-empty (implicitly enforced: if the array is empty, "some index, entry in input" has no bindings and the rule body cannot succeed — scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload is intentionally true for both empty and non-empty arrays).' This prevents Phase-2 implementation error. Alternatively, if the spec text is purely behavioral (not implementation-prescriptive), add a note: '(Note: this condition is implied by the third set of conditions — if no entry exists, the rule has nothing to evaluate.)'.

findings.description: §6.3 line 227 states: 'Both engines use the same regex pattern syntax (`https?://\S+` — `\S` = non-whitespace, matches both engines' regex flavor).' This is largely correct for the ASCII fixture corpus, but there is a subtle Unicode-whitespace divergence: Python 3 re module treats \S as Unicode-aware by default (re.UNICODE flag is on for str patterns), so Python's \S does not match Unicode whitespace characters (e.g. U+00A0 NO-BREAK SPACE, U+2003 EM SPACE). OPA/RE2's [^\s] set is restricted to the ASCII whitespace characters [ \t\n\r\f\v] — it does NOT include Unicode whitespace. A URL containing a Unicode whitespace character would be parsed differently: OPA would match further into the string while Python would stop earlier. For the named fixture corpus (all ASCII URLs) this is irrelevant, but the claim 'matches both engines' regex flavor' is imprecise.
findings.recommendation: Inline fix (low-urgency): add a qualification to §6.3 line 227: 'For the ASCII fixture corpus, both engines agree. A future fixture with Unicode whitespace in a URL-like string may surface a Unicode-whitespace divergence (Python re \S is Unicode-aware; OPA RE2 \S is ASCII-only) — log as TF-020L-001 if encountered during Phase-2 implementation.' Alternatively, file as TF-020L-001 with closure path: if Phase-2 testing surfaces no such divergence on the SCP self-dogfood gate, close TF-020L-001 as no-op.
